content:
# Design Document

## Overview

`tighter-reviews` extends the `review-task prepare` flow and the per-runner config surface in `spec-workflow-mcp` along three independent tracks that share two integration points (`handlePrepare` in `src/tools/review-task.ts`, settings reads in `src/multi-server.ts`):

- **Track A — Typecheck pre-computation**: `handlePrepare` runs `tsc --noEmit` once and surfaces tagged diagnostics + coverage in the response, instead of asking the reviewer to hunt for type errors.
- **Track B — Diff-first context**: `handlePrepare` returns a `git diff -U10 -M HEAD --` of the in-scope files, so the reviewer reads changed hunks instead of full files. A new shared **path denylist** filters secrets/locks/binaries from both diff and hygiene paths.
- **Track C — Per-runner model selection**: a new `resolveRunnerModel(settings, runner)` helper resolves a grouped `adversarial: { model } / taskReview: { model }` shape with a legacy fallback. A small in-process settings cache (`mtime + size`-keyed) keeps repeated reads cheap.

The new `data` fields (`diff`, `diffStats`, `skippedPaths`, `diffTruncated`, `typecheckResults`) are additive; `filesToReview`, `hygieneSignals`, `methodology`, `taskContext`, `implementationSummary`, `steeringExcerpt` keep their current shape.

`buildReviewMethodology` grows new directives (R4.1, R4.2, R4.4–R4.7) that compose with the existing item-9 hygiene directive. Composite output is pinned axis-by-axis against fixture files (R4.10), with two cross-axis fixtures to catch directive redundancy/contradiction.

The orchestration in `handlePrepare` uses **`Promise.allSettled`**, not `Promise.all` — every utility's rejection is converted at the orchestration boundary to its documented absent-with-reason state, preserving the "never throws out of `handlePrepare`" contract under utility failure.

## Steering Document Alignment

### Technical Standards (tech.md)

There is no `tech.md` steering doc in this repo today. Defaults applied:
- TypeScript ESM, Node `child_process` (`execFile`) for shelling out — matches existing `src/core/git-utils.ts` style.
- Vitest with co-located `__tests__/` directories — matches `src/core/__tests__/hygiene-signals.test.ts`.
- No new runtime dependencies; `tsc` invoked via `node_modules/.bin/tsc`, never imported as a library.

### Project Structure (structure.md)

There is no `structure.md` steering doc. Conventions inferred from the tree:
- Pure async utilities live in `src/core/`. New modules (`task-diff.ts`, `typecheck.ts`, `path-denylist.ts`, `adversarial-settings.ts`) follow that pattern.
- Tool handlers live in `src/tools/`. `handlePrepare` stays the only orchestrator; the new utilities are called from it, not from `src/dashboard/`.
- Test fixtures: introduce `src/tools/__tests__/__fixtures__/methodology/` (new — no `__fixtures__` directory exists today; this is the first).

## Code Reuse Analysis

### Existing Components to Leverage

- **`computeHygieneSignals`** (`src/core/hygiene-signals.ts:45`) — extended to consume the new `path-denylist` filter before scanning. Its public signature is unchanged; the denylist is applied internally.
- **`PathUtils`** (`src/core/path-utils.ts`) — used as-is for `getWorkflowRoot`. No additions.
- **`AdversarialRunner.run` / `TaskReviewRunner.run`** (`src/dashboard/adversarial-runner.ts:63`, `src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:58`) — already accept `model?: string` and forward it as `--model`. No signature change. Track C only changes which value is passed.
- **`handlePrepare`** (`src/tools/review-task.ts:118`) — gains a `Promise.allSettled` shell after `allFiles` is computed (line 180). Track A lands the shell; Track B slots the diff utility into the existing seam.
- **`buildReviewMethodology`** (`src/tools/review-task.ts:360`) — gains new arguments (see Components and Interfaces) and emits new directives composed with the existing item-9 hygiene directive (line 422–426).

### Integration Points

- **`multi-server.ts` settings-read callsites**: lines 780–791 (adversarial initial), 948–959 (adversarial retry), 1730–1742 (task-review initial), 1774–1786 (task-review retry). All four sites switch to `resolveRunnerModel(settings, runner)`. The retry paths intentionally call the same resolver (R3.9).
- **`adversarial-settings.json` schema**: extended to optionally include `adversarial: { model }`, `taskReview: { model }`, and `features: { typecheck }`. Legacy top-level `model`, `cli`, `cliArgs` continue to work indefinitely.
- **MCP response schema**: permissive (`additionalProperties` allowed). New optional fields ship without a version bump.

## Architecture

`handlePrepare` orchestrates three pre-computation utilities concurrently via `Promise.allSettled`. Each utility owns its external-process invocation, denylist application, and unavailable/timeout fallbacks. Each utility's contract says it "never throws," but the orchestrator does **not trust** that contract — every rejection is caught and converted to the documented absent-with-reason state.

```mermaid
graph TD
    HP[handlePrepare] --> AF[allFiles from impl log]
    AF --> POOL[Promise.allSettled]
    POOL --> DIFF[computeTaskDiff]
    POOL --> TC[runProjectTypecheck]
    POOL --> HYG[computeHygieneSignals]
    DIFF --> DL1[partitionPaths]
    HYG --> DL1
    DIFF --> GIT1[git diff -U10 -M HEAD --]
    DIFF --> GIT2[git diff --numstat HEAD --]
    TC --> TSC[tsc --noEmit -p . --listFiles]
    POOL --> CONVERT[per-utility rejection to degraded state]
    CONVERT --> BM[buildReviewMethodology]
    BM --> FIX[fixture-pinned composite output]

    MS[multi-server.ts callsites] --> RRM[resolveRunnerModel]
    RRM --> CACHE[settings cache mtime+size]
    RRM --> AR[AdversarialRunner.run]
    RRM --> TR[TaskReviewRunner.run]
```

**Latency framing.** Concurrent execution of the three async utilities themselves means their wall-clock cost is `max(diff, typecheck, hygiene)`, not their sum. Pre-work (settings load, including a potential cold first-call read) and post-work (path normalization, diagnostic tagging) add **linearly** on top of that bound. The "max not sum" claim applies to the three async utilities only, not to end-to-end prepare latency.

### Modular Design Principles

- **Single File Responsibility**: each new utility owns one concern (diff, typecheck, denylist, settings resolution).
- **Component Isolation**: `handlePrepare` is the only orchestrator; utilities don't call each other except through the shared `path-denylist` module.
- **Service Layer Separation**: process spawning lives inside utilities; `handlePrepare` and `multi-server.ts` never call `execFile` or `spawn` directly for these concerns.
- **Utility Modularity**: denylist match logic is one module consumed by two callers (diff, hygiene). To prevent divergent ad-hoc filtering, only the partitioning entry point (`partitionPaths`) is exported. The per-element check stays internal.

## Components and Interfaces

### `src/core/path-denylist.ts` (new)

- **Purpose:** decide whether an absolute path is denylisted from review surfaces (diff, hygiene). Single public entry point so callers can't drift.
- **Public interface:**
  ```ts
  export function partitionPaths(paths: string[]): { kept: string[]; skipped: string[] };
  export const TEST_FIXTURE_SEGMENTS: readonly string[];
  ```
  The per-element decision function is **not** exported. If a future caller needs it, they get it via a follow-up that adds an explicit consistency test pinning `partitionPaths(xs).kept === xs.filter(...)` for arbitrary `xs`.
- **Match semantics (R1.5):** exact basename, basename suffix, basename prefix, path-segment match. NOT glob; NOT git pathspec wildcards.
- **Case-folding rules:**
  - **Secret-bearing basenames, suffixes, prefixes** (`*.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `.env`, `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `.pypirc`) are **always** case-folded. False positives on uppercase like `.ENV` on a Linux case-sensitive volume are harmless; missed matches are not.
  - **Lock-file basenames and binary-suffix entries** (`package-lock.json`, `*.lock`, `*.snap`, `*.min.js`, `*.min.css`, `*.map`) are case-folded only on case-insensitive volumes (`process.platform === 'darwin' || 'win32'`). On Linux these stay case-sensitive — collisions are rare and the cost of a missed match is review noise, not a leak.
  - **Path-segment matches** (`secrets`, `credentials`, `.aws`, `.kube`, `.docker`) are unconditionally case-insensitive (R1.5).
- **Test-fixture exception (R1.6, narrowed):** when any path segment matches `TEST_FIXTURE_SEGMENTS` (`__tests__`, `__fixtures__`, `fixtures`, `test-data`, `testdata`, case-insensitive), the path is **only** exempted from the **path-segment denylist** (`secrets`, `credentials`, `.aws`, `.kube`, `.docker`). The exact-basename, suffix, and prefix rules continue to apply. So `__tests__/__fixtures__/credentials/foo.json` is kept (path-segment carve-out), but `__tests__/__fixtures__/.env` is still denylisted (basename match), and `__tests__/__fixtures__/id_rsa.fixture` is still denylisted (prefix match).
- **Dependencies:** `node:path` only.
- **Reuses:** none.

### `src/core/task-diff.ts` (new)

- **Purpose:** produce a unified diff and numstat of in-scope working-tree changes vs. `HEAD`, with truncation, binary-section stripping, and disambiguated truncation messaging.
- **Interfaces:**
  ```ts
  export type TaskDiffResult = {
    diff: string;
    stats: { filesChanged: number; linesAdded: number; linesRemoved: number } | undefined;
    skippedPaths: string[];
    truncated: boolean;
  };
  export async function computeTaskDiff(
    projectPath: string,
    allFiles: string[]
  ): Promise<TaskDiffResult>;
  ```
- **Behavior:**
  1. `partitionPaths(allFiles)` → kept + skipped.
  2. Run `git diff -U10 -M HEAD --` and `git diff --numstat HEAD --` concurrently with `cwd: projectPath`, `env: { ...process.env, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS: '0' }`, kept paths as pathspec, **`maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024`** on both invocations.
  3. Strip `Binary files ... differ` sections from the unified diff body.
  4. Apply truncation in two phases (R1.9):
     - **Per-file cap** (500 added+removed lines, counted from numstat): replace the file's hunks with `<diff truncated: <file> per-file cap exceeded>` and set `truncated: true`.
     - **Total cap** (50,000 bytes of remaining diff body): if still over budget after per-file truncation, replace remaining files in pathspec order with `<diff truncated: <file> total budget exhausted, file truncated despite size>` and set `truncated: true`.
  5. On any failure (`execFile` rejection, non-zero exit, `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER`, not a git repo, `git` missing) return `{ diff: '', stats: undefined, skippedPaths, truncated: false }`. Never throws.
- **Dependencies:** `node:child_process` (`execFile`), `path-denylist`.
- **Reuses:** `path-denylist.partitionPaths`.

### `src/core/typecheck.ts` (new)

- **Purpose:** run `tsc --noEmit` once per `handlePrepare`, return tagged diagnostics + coverage in the discriminated union shape from R2.2, with denylist-filtered output paths.
- **Interfaces:**
  ```ts
  export type TypecheckDiagnostic = {
    file: string; line: number; column: number;
    code: string; message: string; inScope: boolean;
  };
  export type TypecheckResult =
    | { tsconfigPath: string; status: 'success';
        diagnostics: TypecheckDiagnostic[];
        coverage: { compiled: string[]; excluded: string[] };
        suppressedDenylistedFiles?: number;
        truncated?: boolean }
    | { tsconfigPath: string; status: 'unavailable';
        reason: 'no-tsconfig' | 'project-references' | 'wrapper-config'
              | 'tsc-not-found' | 'no-parseable-output' | 'output-overflow'
              | 'feature-disabled' }
    | { tsconfigPath: string; status: 'timeout' };
  export async function runProjectTypecheck(
    projectPath: string,
    allFiles: string[],
    opts: { enabled: boolean }
  ): Promise<TypecheckResult[]>;
  ```
- **Behavior:**
  1. If `opts.enabled === false` → return `[{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'feature-disabled', tsconfigPath: <root>/tsconfig.json }]`.
  2. Resolve `tsconfig.json` at project root. If missing, has top-level `references`, or is `files: []` with no `include` → return `'no-tsconfig'` / `'project-references'` / `'wrapper-config'` accordingly.
  3. Resolve `tsc` from `<projectPath>/node_modules/.bin/tsc`. If absent → `'tsc-not-found'`.
  4. Spawn `tsc --noEmit -p <projectPath> --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile <projectPath>/.spec-workflow/.cache/tsc.tsbuildinfo --listFiles --pretty false` with `env: { ...process.env, FORCE_COLOR: '0', NO_COLOR: '1' }`, **`maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024`**, and a 30 s timeout (SIGTERM → 2 s grace → SIGKILL).
  5. On timeout → `{ status: 'timeout' }`.
  6. On `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER` → `{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'output-overflow' }`. Distinct from `'no-parseable-output'` so the user sees that the tsc invocation itself was killed mid-output, not that the output couldn't be parsed.
  7. **Parse stdout in two strict passes:**
     - **Pass 1** (diagnostics): match each line against `^(.+?)\((\d+),(\d+)\): error TS(\d+): (.+)$`. Lines that match are diagnostics. Lines that don't are *not yet* listFiles entries.
     - **Pass 2** (listFiles): from the leftover lines, keep only those matching an absolute-path shape (Windows: `^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]`; POSIX: `^/`). Drop everything else (multi-line continuation messages, error-message text containing absolute paths inside a quoted string, blank lines).
     - This guarantees continuation lines from wrapped diagnostics don't pollute the `compiled` set, and that diagnostic prose containing path-shaped substrings doesn't either.
  8. If non-zero exit and zero diagnostics parse → `'no-parseable-output'`. If clean exit and zero `--listFiles` lines → `'no-parseable-output'` (R2.9).
  9. **Async path normalization** (R2.4 with the sync-blocking concern fixed):
     - Normalize both `allFiles` and the `--listFiles` output via `fs.promises.realpath` in chunks of 100 (`Promise.all` over each chunk, sequenced across chunks to bound concurrent FDs).
     - Per-path `try/catch`: on ENOENT (file deleted between log-implementation and prepare) the path is treated as unresolvable and bucketed into `coverage.excluded` with its original `allFiles` form. No throw.
     - Case-folded to lowercase on case-insensitive volumes (`process.platform === 'darwin' || 'win32'`). Per-volume case-sensitivity probing is out of scope for v1 (see "Out of Scope (v2)").
  10. Compute `coverage.compiled = allFiles ∩ listFilesOutput` (normalized form), `coverage.excluded = allFiles \ listFilesOutput`. The reported arrays use the **original `allFiles` paths**, deduped by normalized form, preserving first-seen original.
  11. Tag each diagnostic with `inScope: file ∈ normalizedAllFiles`.
  12. **Denylist-filter the output** (closes the path-leak inconsistency): apply `partitionPaths` to `coverage.compiled`, `coverage.excluded`, and `diagnostics[].file`. Paths that fail the denylist are removed from `coverage.compiled`, removed from `coverage.excluded`, and corresponding diagnostics are dropped. The count of dropped denylisted files is surfaced as `suppressedDenylistedFiles: number`. Note: the compile itself is not filtered (tsc still compiles those files); only the **emitted output** is filtered.
  13. Cap diagnostics at 100 (in-scope first, then out-of-scope), set `truncated: true` if capped.
- **Dependencies:** `node:child_process`, `node:fs/promises`, `node:path`, `path-denylist`.

### `src/core/adversarial-settings.ts` (new)

- **Purpose:** parse `.spec-workflow/adversarial-settings.json` once per `(path, mtime, size)` and resolve per-runner model precedence.
- **Interfaces:**
  ```ts
  export type RunnerKey = 'adversarial' | 'taskReview';
  export type AdversarialSettings = {
    adversarial?: { model?: string } | null;
    taskReview?: { model?: string } | null;
    features?: { typecheck?: boolean } | null;
    model?: string;
    cli?: string;
    cliArgs?: string[];
  };
  export function loadSettings(projectPath: string): AdversarialSettings;
  export function resolveRunnerModel(
    settings: AdversarialSettings,
    runner: RunnerKey
  ): string | undefined;
  export function isTypecheckEnabled(settings: AdversarialSettings): boolean;
  ```
- **Behavior:**
  - **`loadSettings`**: in-process cache keyed by `(absPath, mtime, size)`. **Cold first-call**: on a process's first read, the cache is empty and the helper does a `statSync` + `readFileSync` + `JSON.parse` — typically 5–15 ms; tens of milliseconds on contended Windows mounts. Warm-cache reads are < 1 ms. The "negligible" claim under §Performance applies to warm reads; the cold path is bounded by the underlying I/O.
  - Both `mtime` and `size` must match the stored entry to use the cache (R3.7 — covers second-resolution mtime filesystems). Malformed JSON or top-level non-object → return `{}` and log a warning **once per process per file path**, with the warning flag cleared if and only if `(mtime, size)` advances. Same-second + same-size edits collide on the cache; recovery is documented in user-facing docs (`touch` the file or restart MCP server).
  - **`resolveRunnerModel`**:
    1. If `settings[runner]` is an object with a non-empty string `model` → return it.
    2. Otherwise if top-level `settings.model` is a non-empty string → return it.
    3. Otherwise → `undefined`.
    4. `null`, missing, empty-string, non-object `settings[runner]`, non-string `model` are all treated as absent (R3.5–R3.6). Non-object `settings[runner]` logs a malformed-load warning.
  - **`isTypecheckEnabled`**: returns `true` unless `settings.features?.typecheck === false`. Anything else (missing, null, empty string, non-boolean) → `true` (R3.12).
- **Dependencies:** `node:fs`, `node:path`.

### `src/core/hygiene-signals.ts` (modified)

- **Change:** before scanning, filter `files` through `partitionPaths`. Files in `partitionPaths(files).skipped` are not scanned.
- **Public signature unchanged** (`computeHygieneSignals(files: string[]): Promise<HygieneSignal[]>`).
- **Skipped paths are NOT surfaced from the hygiene path** (they're surfaced from diff via `data.skippedPaths`). This avoids double-reporting the same skip.

### `src/tools/review-task.ts` — `handlePrepare` (modified)

- After `allFiles` is computed (review-task.ts:180), settings load + concurrent utility orchestration:
  ```ts
  const settings = loadSettings(projectPath);
  const settled = await Promise.allSettled([
    computeTaskDiff(projectPath, allFiles),
    runProjectTypecheck(projectPath, allFiles, { enabled: isTypecheckEnabled(settings) }),
    computeHygieneSignals(allFiles),
  ]);
  const diffResult        = unwrapDiff(settled[0]);          // rejection → emptyDiff
  const typecheckResults  = unwrapTypecheck(settled[1]);     // rejection → [{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'no-parseable-output' }]
  const hygieneSignals    = unwrapHygiene(settled[2]);       // rejection → []
  ```
- Each `unwrap*` helper inspects the `PromiseSettledResult`, returns the resolved value if `status === 'fulfilled'`, or constructs the documented absent-with-reason value if `status === 'rejected'` (and logs the rejection reason once per process for debuggability — same warn-once mechanism as the settings loader).
- Adds new fields to `data`:
  ```ts
  data: {
    /* existing */
    taskContext, implementationSummary, steeringExcerpt,
    filesToReview: allFiles,
    hygieneSignals,
    methodology,
    /* new */
    diff: diffResult.diff,
    diffStats: diffResult.stats,
    skippedPaths: diffResult.skippedPaths,
    diffTruncated: diffResult.truncated,
    typecheckResults,
  }
  ```
- **Track A landing**: only `typecheckResults` is added; the `Promise.allSettled` shell is in place but with `Promise.resolve(emptyDiff)` in the diff slot. **Track B landing**: replaces the placeholder with `computeTaskDiff` and adds the diff fields.

### `src/tools/review-task.ts` — `buildReviewMethodology` (modified)

- New signature:
  ```ts
  function buildReviewMethodology(
    taskContext: { /* unchanged */ },
    hasTechSteering: boolean,
    hasPriorReviews: boolean,
    hasHygieneSignals: boolean,
    diffState: 'present' | 'present-truncated' | 'empty',
    typecheckState: TypecheckMethodologyState
  ): string;
  type TypecheckMethodologyState =
    | { kind: 'success-clean-full' }
    | { kind: 'success-with-diagnostics' }
    | { kind: 'success-partial-coverage' }
    | { kind: 'unavailable' }
    | { kind: 'timeout' };
  ```
- **Numbering scheme (resolved):** the diff directive is rendered as an **unnumbered preamble** labeled `**Read first:**` at the top of the methodology. The existing item-1–8 numbering is preserved unchanged. Item 9 hygiene keeps its slot. Typecheck directives are rendered as **item 10** when present. This is the only scheme that preserves existing item references and reads naturally.
- **Directive composition order** (R4.8):
  1. `**Read first:**` preamble — diff directive (R4.1 or R4.2).
  2. Existing items 1–8 unchanged.
  3. Item 9 hygiene (existing) unchanged.
  4. **Item 10 typecheck** (new) — R4.4, R4.5 (composed with R4.4 when partial coverage), R4.6, or R4.7 depending on `typecheckState`. Emitted only if not `success-clean-full`.
- **Caller** (`handlePrepare`) computes `diffState` and `typecheckState` from the pre-computed results and passes them in.

### `src/multi-server.ts` (modified)

- Four callsites switch to `resolveRunnerModel(settings, runner)`:
  - L780–791 (adversarial initial): `runner = 'adversarial'`.
  - L948–959 (adversarial retry): `runner = 'adversarial'`. Same value as initial because `loadSettings` returns the cached parse for unchanged files (R3.9).
  - L1730–1742 (task-review initial): `runner = 'taskReview'`.
  - L1774–1786 (task-review retry): `runner = 'taskReview'`.
- `cli` and `cliArgs` continue to read top-level `settings.cli` / `settings.cliArgs` unchanged.

## Data Models

### `AdversarialSettings` (file shape)

```jsonc
{
  "adversarial": { "model": "claude-opus-4-7" },
  "taskReview":  { "model": "claude-haiku-4-5" },
  "features":    { "typecheck": true },
  "model":       "claude-sonnet-4-6",
  "cli":         "claude",
  "cliArgs":     ["--print", "..."]
}
```

All sub-keys are optional. Unknown keys are silently ignored both at the top level (within reason — non-object `adversarial`/`taskReview`/`features` warn) and within runner / `features` blocks (R3.5, R3.12).

### `data.diff` shape

```ts
{
  diff: string;            // unified diff or ""
  diffStats?: { filesChanged: number; linesAdded: number; linesRemoved: number };
  skippedPaths: string[];
  diffTruncated: boolean;
}
```

`diffStats` is omitted when `diff === ""`.

### `data.typecheckResults` shape

`TypecheckResult[]` — see `src/core/typecheck.ts` interface above. Length is always 1 in v1; future multi-config support adds entries without a schema break. The `suppressedDenylistedFiles` count surfaces output-side denylist filtering.

## Error Handling

### Error Scenarios

1. **`git` missing / not a git repo / `git diff` non-zero exit / `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER`**
   - **Handling:** `computeTaskDiff` catches all `execFile` rejection shapes, returns `{ diff: '', stats: undefined, skippedPaths, truncated: false }`. Never throws.
   - **User Impact:** `data.diff === ""`, methodology emits the diff-empty fallback directive (R4.2). Review continues with `filesToReview`.

2. **`tsc` missing / `tsconfig.json` absent or unsupported**
   - **Handling:** `runProjectTypecheck` returns one `{ status: 'unavailable', reason }` entry.
   - **User Impact:** methodology emits R4.6 (typecheck-unavailable). Review continues.

3. **`tsc` exceeds 30 s**
   - **Handling:** SIGTERM, 2 s grace, SIGKILL. Result is `{ status: 'timeout' }`.
   - **User Impact:** methodology emits R4.7. R4.7 names the kill switch (`features.typecheck: false`) so the user can opt out if the timeout recurs.

4. **`tsc` stdout exceeds maxBuffer (16 MB)**
   - **Handling:** distinct from non-parseable output — result is `{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'output-overflow' }`. The reviewer sees that tsc was killed mid-output, not that the output couldn't be parsed.
   - **User Impact:** methodology emits R4.6 with the specific reason; user knows to either disable typecheck or report the case.

5. **`tsc` exits non-zero with no parseable output, OR clean exit with empty `--listFiles`**
   - **Handling:** result is `{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'no-parseable-output' }`.
   - **User Impact:** methodology emits R4.6.

6. **Diff per-file or total truncation cap exceeded**
   - **Handling:** two distinct messages — `<diff truncated: <file> per-file cap exceeded>` (file's own changes too large) vs `<diff truncated: <file> total budget exhausted, file truncated despite size>` (small file lost a budget race).
   - **User Impact:** reviewer can tell which constraint fired and why; methodology directive notes truncation.

7. **Malformed `adversarial-settings.json`**
   - **Handling:** offending field is ignored as if absent; warning emitted once per process per file path; settings cache stores the partially-parsed result so re-warns happen only after `(mtime, size)` advances.
   - **User Impact:** runner falls back through R3 precedence (legacy `model` → `undefined`). No crash.

8. **Concurrent editor `git status` holding the index lock**
   - **Handling:** `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` env on both `git diff` invocations.
   - **User Impact:** `git diff` proceeds without waiting on the lock.

9. **Symlinked workspace paths (pnpm) producing false `excluded` entries**
   - **Handling:** R2.4 normalization (`fs.promises.realpath` chunked + case-fold on case-insensitive volumes) on both sides of the set ops.
   - **User Impact:** coverage matches user expectation; pinned by a fixture test.

10. **ENOENT during normalization (file deleted between log-implementation and prepare)**
    - **Handling:** per-path `try/catch` inside the chunked `realpath` loop. Unresolvable paths are bucketed into `coverage.excluded` using the original path; the failure is logged once.
    - **User Impact:** the typecheck result still resolves; the deleted file shows up as excluded with no spurious `'no-parseable-output'` reason.

11. **A utility throws unexpectedly (escape from its "never throws" contract)**
    - **Handling:** `Promise.allSettled` in `handlePrepare` catches the rejection. The corresponding `unwrap*` helper converts it to the documented absent-with-reason state (`emptyDiff`, `{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'no-parseable-output' }`, or `[]` for hygiene). The rejection reason is logged once per process.
    - **User Impact:** prepare succeeds with the offending utility's section showing the degraded state. The whole prepare does not fail.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Testing

**Vitest, co-located in `__tests__/`.**

- `src/core/__tests__/path-denylist.test.ts` — exact basename, suffix, prefix, path-segment, case-folding rules per category (secret-bearing always-folded vs lock/binary platform-conditional vs path-segment unconditionally-insensitive), narrowed test-fixture exception (path-segment carve-out only; basename/suffix/prefix rules still fire under fixture paths), binary tagging. ### End-to-End Testing

- **Manual E2E**: invoke `review-task action: prepare` against a small TypeScript fixture repo with uncommitted changes and at least one TS error in scope. Confirm dashboard renders the new fields and the methodology emits the expected directives. Repeat with `features.typecheck: false` to confirm kill-switch path and that R4.7's text reaches the LLM verbatim.
- **Multi-server settings E2E**: edit `.spec-workflow/adversarial-settings.json` mid-session, trigger an adversarial review and a task review, confirm each runner gets its respective `--model` from the grouped shape; remove the grouped shape and confirm legacy `model` is used; remove all model fields and confirm no `--model` flag is passed. **Note**: mid-session edit reliability is verified by the automated `utimes()` test (Unit Testing above); the manual E2E here is for the multi-runner dispatch path, not for the cache invalidation path.
- No automated E2E harness exists in this repo today; manual E2E remains the convention.

## Out of Scope (v2)

These were raised during adversarial review and deliberately deferred. Documented here so they aren't lost.

- **Content-hash third cache key for `(mtime, size)` collisions.** Same-second + same-size edits to `adversarial-settings.json` strand the cache on the prior parse. Recovery is `touch` the file or restart the MCP server. The README's R3.11 documentation block calls this out as a known cache-miss recovery path. A content-hash third key is ~10 lines but unmotivated until users actually report it.
- **Per-volume case-sensitivity probe on macOS APFS.** `process.platform === 'darwin'` always treats macOS as case-insensitive, which is wrong for the (rare) APFS case-sensitive volumes. v1 ships the platform default; the typecheck.ts comment header references R2.4's "OR by reading the platform's reported case sensitivity if a more reliable signal is available" wording so a future PR has a concrete hook.
- **`features.typecheckRequired: true` fail-loud setting.** Lets a project flip R4.6 from soft directive to hard prepare-fail. Useful for projects that consider type-checking a hard precondition; v1's binary kill switch can't express it. Genuinely new feature surface; defer to a follow-up.
- **Property-based test for the path-denylist matcher.** `fast-check` is a useful addition for the fixture-exception negation rule, but it's a new dev dependency. v1 uses hand-written cases at the boundaries (basename/suffix/prefix interaction with fixture-exception). A follow-up can add `fast-check` if matcher edges surface in practice.
- **Structured dashboard tag for typecheck degradation.** `data.typecheckResults[0].status` is already structured; whether the dashboard renders a pill from it is a UI concern outside this spec. Defer.

## Non-Functional Requirements (notes carried from requirements.md, refined)

- **Performance / settings load**: warm-cache reads < 1 ms; cold first-call read 5–15 ms typical, up to tens of ms on contended Windows mounts. The performance claim in requirements.md (`< 5 ms per call`) applies to warm reads; first-call cost is bounded by the underlying I/O, not by cache machinery.
- **Performance / path normalization**: chunked async `fs.promises.realpath` (100 paths per chunk) keeps the event loop free during the otherwise-blocking step. End-to-end normalization for a 5,000-file monorepo is bounded by `ceil(5000/100) * (per-chunk wall-clock)` rather than by the synchronous sum.
- **Reliability / orchestration**: `Promise.allSettled` is the orchestration primitive in `handlePrepare`. The "never throws" contract on each utility is enforced at the orchestrator boundary, not relied upon.
- **Reliability / buffer overflow**: both `git diff` and `tsc` invocations specify `maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024`. Overflow degrades to a documented absent-with-reason state with a distinct sub-reason.
